region.text: Gorodets Meshchersky and its district on the Oka

ledger.note: 1452: Vasily II gives Gorodets Meshchersky to the Kazan prince Qasim, founding the Qasim Khanate. 'The khanate was established in the lands which Grand Prince Vasily II of Moscow (r. 1425-1462) presented in 1452'; Kasimov page: 'In 1452, Great Duke Vasily II of the Grand Duchy of Moscow gave this town to Kazan prince Qasim Khan.' The page names the town and district, not a boundary; the Cliopatria 1453 shape stands for the district.

ledger.note: 1502: a sliver on the south-east edge is added. Page silent: Cliopatria's Qasim shape grows by 1,264 km2 in 1502, the year the Golden Horde ends, all inside the Golden Horde's 1501 shape.

region.text: the district of Kasimov on the middle Oka

ledger.note: 1681: the Qasim Khanate is abolished. 'After the death of khanbika (queen) Fatima Soltan in 1681, the Khanate was abolished'; Kasimov page: 'It remained the capital of Qasim Khanate until 1681 when the khanate was absorbed into Russia.'

wars.name: Russo-Kazan War of 1467-1469
wars.outcome: 'Ivan failed to get Qasim on the throne of Kazan, and had to recognise Ibrahim as the legitimate successor'; the 1469 treaty followed and 'Qasim died soon after'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Qasim, uncle of Ibrahim, is called 'the vassal of Ivan III' on the page; the Qasim Khanate page: 'Qasim claimed the Kazan throne in 1467, but the Russo-Kazan War of 1467-1469 failed.'

wars.name: Muscovite siege of Kazan (1487)
wars.outcome: 'Prince Kholmsky sailed down the Volga from Nizhny Novgorod and laid siege to Kazan on 18 May 1487', and 'Moxammat Amin was proclaimed the new khan'. Qasim khans with their guard took part in the raids of 1467-1469, 1487 and 1552 (Qasim Khanate page).

wars.name: Russian conquest of Kazan (1552)
wars.outcome: 'the final siege of the Tatar capital commenced on 30 August' and 'the final storming on 2 October led to the taking of the city of Kazan'; 'Shahghali took part in the final Russian conquest of Kazan in 1552' (Shahghali page). The Qasim Khanate gained and lost no land.
wars.note: Shahghali had been Moscow's candidate for the Kazan throne in 1519-1521, 1546 and 1551-1552 (Shahghali page).

certainty.note: A fief on the Oka granted by Moscow; the page gives no boundary survey, so the outline is Cliopatria's approximation throughout.

notes:
Written for batch ia-02-d. Four pages opened (budget 5 for 4 shapes).
Settled: foundation 1452 (page; Cliopatria 1453), capital Kasimov to 1681, abolition in 1681.
Corrected: Cliopatria ends the row in 1551 but the page has the khanate to 1681: new keyframe qasim-khanate_1552 carries the 1547 shape to 1681. Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia shape contains the whole Qasim outline from 1552, so the Russian and Moscow dossiers (eu-16) should carry the vassal tint for the whole life: the Grand Principality / Tsardom as suzerain with vassal_start 1452 and vassal_end 1681, counterpart qasim-khanate (Russo-Kazan page: Qasim 'the vassal of Ivan III'; Shahghali page: 'as a vassal of the Russians'). Otherwise the khanate is drawn twice from 1552.
